name: Katam (Buxus dioica) hair dye

lead: Katam is a dark green leaf powder from Buxus dioica, sold as a plant-based hair dye. It is commonly used in the Middle East alongside henna to cover grey and white hair and to move hair from henna's red-orange toward brown or near-black.

Users pair it with henna because the two stack: henna gives a base colour, katam adds depth with violet-toned darkness rather than the blue tones of indigo. Evidence is limited to retailer and user descriptions; no clinical studies are known.

paras: Sellers describe pretreating grey hair with henna for a period, rinsing, then applying a paste of katam mixed with hot water or tea, left on for roughly 40 to 120 minutes. Colour can deepen over a few hours as it oxidises.

No safety studies of katam as a hair dye were located. Retailers describe it as natural and vegan; one lists it as suitable in pregnancy while advising a doctor's check for concerns. Reviews on retail pages note that some products do not match their description.

angle.text: Katam is a plant colourant used to cover grey and darken hair. Users typically combine it with henna for depth, and the colour is semi-permanent plant staining.

lead: Katam is a powder made from the leaves of Buxus dioica, the Yemeni box tree, sold as an herbal hair colourant. [1] It is used in the Middle East, usually mixed or layered with henna, to cover white and grey hair. [1]

For appearance, katam is used to turn the orange-red of plain henna into deeper brown to near-black tones. One retailer describes the result as almost black with violet undertones, in contrast to the blue undertones of indigo, which is the other plant commonly used for this purpose. [1] Colour can take hours to show fully on dry hair because the plant dye oxidises slowly. [1]
Information about katam comes mainly from retailers; no clinical studies of katam were found, and standard encyclopedic coverage is limited.

paras: Katam is sold as a fine dark green powder listed under the INCI name Buxus Dioica Leaf Powder. [1] Retailers also market it as 'black henna', although other sellers note that it is a distinct plant from henna (Lawsonia). The name can cause confusion with synthetic products sold under the same phrase.

Product guidance for grey hair describes first applying henna for 20 to 45 minutes, rinsing, and then applying katam paste made with hot water or black tea, covered and left on for 40 to 120 minutes depending on the depth desired. [1] The same listing says katam suits brown and dark brown hair and gives light brown hair a dark, cool shade. [1]
Sellers say that on its own katam gives limited colour and that it is mainly used with henna, while others describe stand-alone use for brown shades.

The retailer page markets katam as 100 percent natural, vegan and nickel tested. [1] Reviews on the page include one user who found the product produced copper tones and suspected it was a henna-indigo mix, which illustrates that powders sold under the katam name may differ. [1]
